subject.title: Skill and Read tools truncating output at ~600-700 chars in 2026.6.11

question: Should maintainers require a live packaged v2026.6.11 or current-main reproduction of both the 600-700 character cutoff and Skill Workshop proposal lookup failure before authorizing a cap or persistence fix?
rationale: The obvious OpenClaw and Codex source caps are much higher than the report, and the remaining plausible causes span display sanitization, transcript persistence, model projection, Codex replay, and workspace-scoped proposal lookup.

options.title: Require Live Repro First
options.body: Keep the issue open and block fix automation until a packaged Linux gateway run captures the exact truncation and proposal-state failure with transcript, model-payload, workspace, and state-dir evidence.

options.title: Investigate Source Paths Now
options.body: Assign a maintainer or agent to trace display, embedded-runner, transcript, Codex replay, and Skill Workshop state flows from source before reporter proof, accepting a higher chance of chasing the wrong layer.

options.title: Split The Report
options.body: Treat the read/output portion as related to existing output-projection issues and ask for a separate Skill Workshop proposal-state report, at the cost of splitting a possibly shared packaged-gateway root cause.

recommendation.title: Require Live Repro First
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and block fix automation until a packaged Linux gateway run captures the exact truncation and proposal-state failure with transcript, model-payload, workspace, and state-dir evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent Koc is the best available routing owner from the sampled history because the report crosses the v2026.6.11 release surface, Skill Workshop proposal scoping, and agent/tool runtime behavior.
